setup.pitch: Saltmere’s well still gives water. The water forgets your name.
setup.gmSummary: The well at Saltmere is another Quiet Seal. A name-stone in the cistern was pried loose. The Draught in the water pays for rain with names. Oda Flint sent the party. Mill Kade keeps the well and will lie to save it. Jory Salt drank this morning and cannot say his daughter’s name. Clock: at dusk the bucket comes up dry and the Draught takes a whole household. Five legal endings: reseat the stone, feed a false name, give a true name, smash the well (thirst), or walk away at dusk (a household forgets). No one NPC is required. Campaign fact from Episode 1 (lantern ending) colors how hungry the Draught is, it does not change the graph.
setup.campaignFrame: After Briar Glen, they are back in Hearthford. Oda Flint (mill, building 2) has the next job. Mark her Helped when this night ends.

quest.objective: Stop the well from drinking names before the dusk bucket comes up dry.
quest.stakes: If the bucket is dry at dusk, one household in Saltmere forgets itself.
quest.deadline: Dusk, about four hours after Oda sends them.
successConditions: The Draught is reseated, tricked, paid a true name, destroyed, or the well is smashed on purpose.
Saltmere still has water, or the table chose thirst on purpose.
failureConditions: Dusk, dry bucket, no new arrangement.
The party leaves Saltmere without touching the well or the stone.

facts.text: The well is a Quiet Seal, same family as Briar Glen’s lantern.
A carved name-stone was pried from the cistern wall.
Something in the water — the Draught — buys rain with names.
When the dusk bucket comes up dry, it takes a whole household.

secrets.text: Mill Kade pried the stone because she wanted to forget a fire she caused in Saltmere’s drying shed last winter — not Oda’s mill in Hearthford.
secrets.revealCondition: Confront her with the dry cup, her confession, or the scratch marks matching her well-hook.

npcs.name: Reeve Oda Flint
voiceCues: names the well before she names people
wants: The well keeps water and names
knows: Saltmere’s well has always given more than the rain
Jory drank this morning and could not say his daughter’s name
The dusk bucket is the clock
believes: Mill Kade is tired, not guilty
npcs.questFunction: Starts the night. If dead or refused, her written order on the mill desk and Jory on the road still send them.
npcs.description: A square-faced reeve in a flour-dusted coat, carrying two ledgers and a stoppered sample of well water she has refused to drink all day.
tableDialogue: “The well is still giving water. The trouble is it has started taking names in exchange.”
“At dusk we draw once. If the bucket comes up dry, a household forgets itself.”
“Bring me back a well that still knows who drinks from it. If that is impossible, bring me the truth before dusk.”

reactions.agreement: Pays 50 gp up front, gives directions to the square, and names Jory as the clearest living witness.
reactions.refusal: Hands over the written emergency order anyway; the dusk clock and Jory still make the crisis actionable.
reactions.accusation: Admits she has prioritized grain and water security over the village's folklore but denies knowing who altered the cistern.
reactions.danger: Keeps townsfolk away from the well and prepares wagons for emergency water hauling.

npcs.name: Mill Kade
voiceCues: people call her Mill; the building is the well-house
wants: No one to learn about the fire
fears: Her name on the next bucket
knows: The cistern has a loose stone with a name cut in it
The Draught answers if you speak into the shaft
Four cups on the well-house shelf
believes: If they smash the well, Saltmere dies by autumn
secrets: She pried the name-stone to forget the Saltmere drying-shed fire
lies: At first: the stone fell on its own in the freeze
cannotKnow: Whether a false name will choke the Draught

revealRules.when: Shown the dry cup, the matching hook scratches, or a successful DC 13 Insight after the fire is mentioned.

npcs.questFunction: Local contact and one source for the stone. Not required.
npcs.description: A tired well-keeper with rolled sleeves, a scorched leather glove on one hand, and a ring of iron keys that never stops clicking against her hip.
tableDialogue: “The well gives. That is what matters until someone proves we can live without it.”
“Do not call this building a mill. I keep the well. The mill is miles south and belongs to Oda's people.”
“The stone did not fall. I pulled it. I wanted one night of my life to stop burning.”

reactions.agreement: If promised the well will not simply be smashed, calls the Name-Drowned down and opens the well-house.
reactions.refusal: Bars the well-house but leaves Stealth, force, and the shaft as legal routes; required clues remain physical.
reactions.accusation: Shown the chip or hook scratches, admits she pried the name-stone to forget the drying-shed fire.
reactions.danger: Calls the drowned by no-name if she can and gets behind the well-house wall rather than fighting the party.

npcs.name: Jory Salt
personality: keeps asking you to say his daughter’s name so he can hear it
voiceCues: repeats the last word you said
does not say ‘Lina’ unless you say it first
knows: He drank at dawn and the name left
The well-house has four tin cups

revealRules.fact: Drinking the well takes a name.

npcs.questFunction: Backup clue and talk-out leverage with the Draught (offer Lina’s name only if the table is cruel — print that cost).
npcs.description: A broad-handed laborer seated beside a child's slate, rubbing the same chalked name with his thumb as though friction might make it stay in his memory.
tableDialogue: “Say her name again. Please. I know that face is my daughter. The word will not stay.”
“I drank at dawn. After that, the rope was wet and there were four cups where Mill keeps the keys.”
“If something below needs a true name, I can shout Lina's. Do not pretend that would be free.”

reactions.agreement: Describes the cups and rope clearly and offers to remain near the square if the party later needs his voice.
reactions.refusal: Will not descend and will not volunteer Lina's name, but the physical clues he already described remain available.
reactions.accusation: Does not defend Mill; he says only that guilt and hunger can make people do the same terrible thing for different reasons.
reactions.danger: Takes the child's slate and moves away from the well, but remains close enough to answer if called.

locations.name: Saltmere well-square
locations.description: Twenty roofs, a stone well at center, well-house north, Jory southwest, drying shed northwest, road south to Hearthford.

locations.name: Jory’s cottage
locations.description: One room. A child’s slate with a name written and rubbed out.

locations.name: Well-house
locations.description: Shed over the well. Four tin cups. Trapdoor to the shaft.

locations.name: Cistern
locations.description: Forty-foot circle. Walkway. Dark water 15 feet across. Loose name-stone on the ring.

scenes.title: The Reeve’s Well
scenes.purpose: Oda hires them. Clock is dusk. Seed Saltmere and the missing name.
scenes.readAloud:
Hearthford’s mill smells of wet grain and chalk. Reeve Oda Flint does not sit. She turns a tally-stick in her hands until the numbers face you.

“Saltmere’s well still draws,” she says. “The water does not keep names. Jory Salt drank at dawn and could not say his daughter. Dusk is the bad bucket. If it comes up dry, a house forgets itself. I need you there before that.”

On the desk, already written: an order to Mill Kade, well-keeper, and a note of fifty gold if the well still knows people by nightfall.
gmNotes: Oda is the giver. DC 12 Insight: she is afraid for grain, not for folklore.
If they refuse or kill her, the written order and Jory on the south road still send them. Recovery.
Episode 1 fact: if the lantern was smashed, Oda says the ridge ‘has been thirsty since the flame went’. Cosmetic hunger, same graph.
Pay: 50 gp now, 50 gp when they return with a well that still names people — or with a honest reason it does not.

runSteps.title: Give the job and dusk clock
runSteps.text: Oda pays 50 gp now and 50 gp on return. State plainly that the dusk bucket determines whether another household loses itself.

runSteps.title: Connect the previous night
runSteps.text: Use the Episode 1 outcome only as flavor. The current job remains the well, Jory's lost name, and the dusk deadline.

runSteps.title: Go to Saltmere square
runSteps.text: Send the party to the well rather than keeping the hiring scene in conversation.

scenes.advanceWhen: The party accepts the dusk problem and goes to Saltmere's well square.

scenes.title: The Well That Still Gives
scenes.purpose: Guardian beat. See the well. Fight, sneak, or talk past the Name-Drowned.
scenes.readAloud:
Saltmere is twenty roofs around a stone well. The bucket is wet. The puddle at the lip does not reflect faces — only the sky.

People draw water and do not drink it. They carry it inside and wait. A woman in a waxed coat — Mill Kade — stands between you and the well-house with a hook in her hand.

In the trough, three shapes sit up. They have the outlines of people who drank here and did not get their names back. They do not speak. They mouth words that have no sound.
gmNotes: Name-Drowned: 3 creatures, AC 12, 22 HP. See Encounters. They rise if anyone drinks, attacks the well, or shoves Mill aside. They do not chase past the square.
Talk: Persuasion DC 13 with Mill — she lets them into the well-house if they swear not to break the well. Insight DC 12: she is guilty, not only tired.
Bypass: Stealth DC 12 group along the drying-shed wall into the well-house. Failure starts the fight 15 feet from the well.
Jory’s cottage is southwest if they ask where the man who forgot a child lives.
Mill is a person (Millicent Kade). Do not call the well-house “the mill.” Oda’s mill is in Hearthford.

runSteps.title: Show the well before the threat
runSteps.text: Put Mill, the trough, the well-house, and Jory's southwest cottage in view. Let players decide whether to speak, sneak, inspect, or drink.

runSteps.title: Resolve the guardian job
runSteps.text: Use Mill's Persuasion route, group Stealth, or the Name-Drowned encounter. The party only needs access to the well-house/shaft.

runSteps.title: Choose the investigation route
runSteps.text: They may question Jory, enter the Four Cups room, or force a direct descent if they have a way down.

scenes.advanceWhen: The party gains access to the well-house/shaft or deliberately goes to Jory for more information.

scenes.title: The Name That Would Not Stay
scenes.purpose: Backup clues. Jory. Optional. Not a hinge.
scenes.readAloud:
Jory Salt has the door open. A girl of seven sits on the step with a slate. The slate says LINA in a child’s hand. Jory looks at it as if it were a map of a country he has not visited.

“I know she is mine,” he says. “I do not know the sound. If you go down the well, do not drink. The bucket is a mouth.”
gmNotes: He describes the four cups and the wet rope. That is clue-cups physical backup.
He will not go down. He will shout ‘LINA’ from the square if they need a true name at the cistern — that is a cost. Record it.
If they skip this scene, the slate is still visible from the square (physical).

runSteps.title: Make the loss personal
runSteps.text: Let Jory ask the party to say Lina's name aloud so he can hear the word he cannot hold.

runSteps.title: Give backup information
runSteps.text: He describes the four cups and wet rope. If asked, he can later shout Lina's name from the square at a real cost.

runSteps.title: Return to the well
runSteps.text: Do not make Jory a hinge. Once the players have what they want, send them back to the well-house.

scenes.advanceWhen: The party has Jory's account and returns to the well investigation.

scenes.title: Four Cups
scenes.purpose: Puzzle beat. Opens the trapdoor honestly.
scenes.readAloud:
The well-house is a shed. Four tin cups sit on a wet shelf, each sweating a name: ODA, JORY, MILL, and one cup that is dry and blank.

The trapdoor to the shaft is barred with a simple wooden latch carved in the same hand as the names. It will not lift while the three wet cups still hold water.
gmNotes: Puzzle: the dry cup is the key. Empty the three wet cups back into the well (or drink — each drink is a name, Wis DC 13 or lose a trivial name until dawn) and the latch opens.
Solution is the dry cup covering a chip of the name-stone. Investigation DC 12 notices the dry ring and the chip.
Fail-forward: smash the latch (Str DC 12). The cups spill; the Name-Drowned in the square, if still up, hear it and climb the roof. The shaft still opens.
Do not let the puzzle eat twenty minutes of guessing. After two wrong tries, tell them the dry cup is wrong in a different way — it is dry because it hid the chip.

runSteps.title: Put all four cups in front of them
runSteps.text: Three are wet and one is dry. The dry cup covers the name-stone chip.

runSteps.title: Resolve or fail forward
runSteps.text: Investigation DC 12 spots the dry ring. Emptying the wet cups or lifting the dry cup works; smashing the latch also opens the shaft with the listed noise consequence.

runSteps.title: Open the shaft
runSteps.text: Once the latch is open, keep the name-stone chip clue in play and move downstairs.

scenes.advanceWhen: The shaft is open and the party has access to the name-stone chip clue.

scenes.title: The Bucket That Drinks
scenes.readAloud:
The shaft is forty feet of wet rungs. A bucket hangs on a new rope, dripping. Names bead on the inside of the tin and slide off before you can read them.

Halfway down, the bucket knocks against a rung as if it were being drawn from below.
gmNotes: Trap: using the bucket or standing on the same rung it strikes. Wisdom DC 13. Failure: 2d6 psychic and your name appears on the next bucket — fiction only, you still have your character sheet. Success: half damage, no name on the tin.
Fail-forward: either way they can keep climbing. The cistern is open.
Athletics DC 12 to climb with no incident if they ignore the bucket (tie it off). Failure means the trap fires once.

runSteps.title: Make the bucket suspicious
runSteps.text: Show names appearing and sliding off the tin before the bucket knocks against the rung.

runSteps.title: Resolve the trap once
runSteps.text: Use the listed Wisdom DC 13 if triggered. Tying off the bucket and climbing is a full solution.

runSteps.title: Reach the cistern
runSteps.text: Whether the trap fires or not, the party continues down. Do not add another obstacle.

scenes.advanceWhen: The party reaches the cistern, whether or not the bucket trap fired.

scenes.title: The Draught
scenes.purpose: Climax. Fight, plug, trick, or feed.
scenes.readAloud:
The cistern is a forty-foot ring of old stone. Water occupies the middle, black and still, fifteen feet across. A carved stone the size of a loaf lies on the walkway, name-side down. The empty socket in the wall weeps.

The water stands up. It has too many mouths and none of them are sure they belong to it.

“Put it back,” the mouths say, “or give me a name that still remembers itself. Or break the ring. I will be very thirsty either way.”
gmNotes: Roll initiative after read-aloud unless they answer immediately with a legal talk-out (then delay initiative).
Draught: AC 14, 72 HP, swim 40. See Encounters.

Five legal jobs: (1) 0 HP. (2) Reseat the name-stone, Athletics or Religion DC 13, three successes. (3) False name, Deception DC 15. (4) True name with permission, Persuasion DC 13. (5) Smash the well-ring, Strength DC 15 — well dies, town thirsty, Draught 0 HP.
Talk-out is real. It wants a name. It does not need to be a boss fight.
Prepared: start at 54 HP. Rushed (skipped cups and Jory): it acts first and the stone is in the water (need a DC 12 Athletics to fetch).

runSteps.title: Let the Draught speak before violence
runSteps.text: After the read-aloud, pause for an answer. Delay initiative if the party immediately attempts a legal bargain or stone solution.

runSteps.title: State the five jobs
runSteps.text: Kill it, reseat the stone, feed a false name, give a true name with permission, or smash the ring. The consequences already written are the consequences.

runSteps.title: Run the chosen pressure
runSteps.text: Use the quick-run stats and checks. Prepared/rushed state changes starting HP and stone position only as written.

runSteps.title: End on a real consequence
runSteps.text: As soon as one legal resolution completes, stop combat and carry that exact well/name state to the square.

scenes.advanceWhen: The Draught is defeated, the stone is reseated, a name bargain succeeds, or the well-ring is broken.

scenes.title: What the Well Remembers
scenes.purpose: Pay, campaign fact, back to Hearthford.
scenes.readAloud:
Dusk on the square. People wait to see whether the bucket comes up with water, with a name, or with nothing.

Oda is on the south road if you go back. She will ask what the well costs now. Mark her Helped. If you kept Mill’s secret, Trusted is a conversation, not an automatic.
gmNotes: Apply the ending. Pay remaining gold if they were honest.
Write the campaign fact on the town page.
Do not start Episode 3 tonight unless the table is still standing and Chris has more nights live.

runSteps.title: Show the bucket result
runSteps.text: Make the ending visible in the square: water, names, thirst, bargain, or loss.

runSteps.title: Pay and record
runSteps.text: Apply the appropriate remaining payment and record the campaign fact, including any true name freely given.

runSteps.title: Close the night
runSteps.text: Return the party toward Hearthford after the consequence is clear. Do not begin the next episode inside this one.

scenes.advanceWhen: The ending, payment, and campaign consequence are recorded.

sources: a record scratched on the well-house wall: DUSK = HOUSE

sources: Oda if they mention Briar Glen
Mill if pressed after the cups

clues.revelation: A name-stone was pried from the cistern wall.

Mill’s hook scratches on the stone
the empty socket in the cistern chamber

clues.revelation: The Draught in the water buys rain with names.

encounters.name: Name-Drowned
encounters.summary: Three wet dead from the trough. They mouth forgotten names.
encounters.resolution: Fight, stealth, or talk Mill into sending them under.
encounters.talkOut: Persuasion DC 13 with Mill: she calls them by no-name and they sit back down. They do not negotiate themselves.
encounters.bypass: Stealth DC 12 group into the well-house. They do not chase past the square.
encounters.special: Ambush if someone drinks from the well. Fight until destroyed or Mill’s talk-out. No pursuit.
encounters.objective: Gain access to the well-house or cross the square without letting the drowned drag the investigation into the well.

encounters.name: The Draught
encounters.summary: A water-that-is-names. Wants a name, a stone, or a broken ring.
encounters.resolution: Kill, reseat the stone, trick with a false name, give a true name, or smash the well.
encounters.talkOut: Deception DC 15 with a false name, or Persuasion DC 13 with a true name freely given. It then withdraws. Record the cost.
encounters.special: Does not leave the cistern. Will negotiate before the first attack if they speak. Smash the ring is Strength DC 15 and ends it, town thirsty.
encounters.objective: End the exchange of water for names through combat, repair, deception, consent, or destruction of the well.

puzzles.name: Four Cups
puzzles.prompt: Three cups sweat names. One is dry and blank. The latch will not lift.
puzzles.solution: The dry cup hides a chip of the name-stone. Empty the wet cups or lift the dry one. Investigation DC 12 notices the dry ring.
puzzles.failForward: Smash the latch (Str DC 12). The shaft opens. The Name-Drowned hear it if still active.

traps.name: The Bucket That Drinks
traps.trigger: Using the bucket or sharing a rung when it knocks.
traps.effect: 2d6 psychic. Failure also writes your name on the next bucket (fiction). Success: half damage, no name.
traps.purpose: Fail-forward: the climb continues either way.

items.name: Name-stone
items.description: A loaf-sized carved stone. One face is a name that will not stay in the mouth.

playMaps.title: Saltmere (player handout)
playMaps.caption: No secrets. Well, mill, road to Hearthford.

playMaps.title: Cistern 40×40
notes: Name-stone on the ring unless rushed (then in the water)

endings.name: The Stone Goes Home
endings.result: The well keeps water and names. Mill’s fire is still a secret unless they told it. Oda Helped.

endings.name: A Name That Was Never Anyone
endings.condition: The Draught accepts a false name.
endings.result: It withdraws, hungry. The well works until the lie wears. Campaign fact: the Draught will ask again in a later night.

endings.name: A Name Freely Given
endings.condition: Someone gives a true name with permission.
endings.result: The Draught sleeps. Record whose name. That person is Bound to Saltmere in a way the town will notice.

endings.name: Thirst
endings.condition: The well-ring is smashed or the Draught is destroyed without reseating.
endings.result: No more names taken. No more extra water. Saltmere hauls from Hearthford. Oda is not pleased and still Helped if they were honest.

endings.name: Let Them Forget
endings.condition: The table walks away before dusk with no new arrangement.
endings.result: The dusk bucket is dry. One household (Jory’s, if they met him) forgets itself. The well still gives. This is a legal, ugly ending.

recovery.principle: No single NPC is required. The ending is never locked.

routes.response: Written mill order and Jory on the south road. Clock still dusk.
Cups, wall tally, and cistern socket still tell the stone story.
The child’s slate is visible from the square. Cups still open the shaft.

routes.trigger: Puzzle smashed or shaft skipped by jumping
routes.response: They land in the cistern. Trap still can fire once. Finale still runs.

pathPressure.principle: Prepared pays. Rush costs. The ending is never locked; they still finish.
prepared: Spoke with Jory: he will shout a name from the square if they ask (cost if it is Lina).
Solved cups without smashing: name-stone starts on the walkway; Draught 54 HP.
rushed: Skipped cups and Jory: stone is in the water (Athletics DC 12 to fetch).
Drank from the well: one PC starts the cistern with a name on the bucket (disadvantage on the first save vs the Draught).

notes: Name-Drowned are original undead, zombie-adjacent, not SRD zombies by name.
Draught original. Psychic damage, Wis saves. No non-SRD spells required.
Same numbers. 2024 pregen pack if the table toggles. No Extra Attack at 4. Paladin smite is a spell.

cutOrder: If 30+ minutes behind, skip Jory as a played scene; leave his slate visible and move his cup/rope information to the square.
If 20+ minutes behind in Four Cups, reveal that the dry cup is hiding something after the first wrong theory rather than waiting for two.
If 15+ minutes behind at the cistern, state all five legal resolution jobs immediately after the Draught speaks.

checks.label: Talk Mill into opening the well-house
checks.success: She sends the Name-Drowned under and unbars the shed. Insight DC 12 along the way: she is guilty.
checks.failure: She refuses. Stealth or a fight still opens the night. Required clues are not lost.

checks.label: Notice the dry cup hides the chip
checks.success: Find the name-stone chip. Latch opens.
checks.failure: They can still empty cups or smash the latch (Str DC 12).

checks.label: Reseat the name-stone
checks.failure: No progress. The acting character is pulled 5 ft toward the water.

checks.label: Feed a false name
checks.failure: It knows. Whispering drink: 3d6 psychic, Wis DC 13 half, and it attacks the speaker.

checks.label: Give a true name with permission
checks.success: The Draught sleeps. Record the name. Ending-true.
checks.failure: It takes a syllable anyway (fiction) and the fight continues. The name is not fully given.

encounters.objective: Cross the square or put the drowned down.
encounters.start: Three Name-Drowned sit up in the trough if the well is threatened, drunk from, or Mill is shoved.
encounters.bypass: Persuasion DC 13 with Mill, or Stealth DC 12 group.

creatures.name: Name-Drowned
creatures.attack: Wet Hands. Melee +4 to hit, reach 5 ft.; 1d6+2 bludgeoning plus the target’s name tastes wrong until end of their next turn (no mechanical penalty unless they drink).
creatures.trait: Does not pursue past the square. Immune to charmed. Vulnerable to fire.
creatures.tactics: Grapple toward the well. Fight until destroyed if Mill has not called them down. Treat as CR 1/4 (50 XP) each; 150 XP total, Low. Talk-out is the intended door.

encounters.end: Destroyed, sat down by Mill, or the party is in the well-house.

encounters.start: The water stands up after the read-aloud. Delay initiative if they answer it immediately.

creatures.name: The Draught
creatures.resistances: acid; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks
creatures.attack: Name Pull. Melee +6 to hit, reach 10 ft.; 2d8+3 psychic and pull 5 ft.
creatures.action: Drinking Whisper. One creature within 60 ft. Wis DC 13; 3d6 psychic and disadvantage on the next check to reseat or deceive. Half damage on success.
creatures.trait: Lair: at initiative 20, the water rises. DC 12 Strength or be pulled 5 ft toward the center.
creatures.tactics: Talk first if they speak. Then target whoever holds the stone. Prepared 54 HP. Does not leave the cistern. CR 4 (1,100 XP) plus lair, High band with the drowned.

encounters.ritual: Reseat: 3 successes on check-stone before 0 HP or dusk.
encounters.bargain: False name check-false DC 15, or true name check-true DC 13.
encounters.destroy: Smash the ring, Strength DC 15, one action if the character is on the walkway. Well dies.
encounters.end: 0 HP, 3 stone successes, a successful name, or a smashed ring.

hazards.trigger: Using the bucket or sharing its rung.
hazards.failure: 2d6 psychic and your name on the next bucket (fiction).

rewards.when: They return with a well that still names people, or an honest thirst.
They keep the leftover chip without reseating a fake.
rewards.reward: A 40 gp moonstone in the well-house box.

rewards.when: Prepared: Jory and cups without smashing.
rewards.reward: Jory sends a loaf and a healer’s kit. Mill, if not denounced, adds 25 gp silence-money.
